plan.target: mstatus.MXR and sstatus.MXR are Incorrectly Writable When Address Translation / Virtual Memory is Disabled (src/privileged/csrsr.sv)
plan.rationale: In `src/privileged/csrsr.sv`, the `mstatus.MXR` and `sstatus.MXR` (Make eXecutable Readable, bit 19) register field is erroneously left writable in configurations where virtual memory is unsupported (e.g. `P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED == 0` under configuration `nodcache_rv64gc`). The RISC-V Instruction Set Manual, Volume II: Privileged Architecture (v20211203), Section 3.1.6.3 explicitly mandates: 'When address translation is not supported (i.e., satp.MODE is read-only 0), MXR is read-only 0.' Section 4.1.1 further reaffirms: 'The MXR and SUM bits are read-only 0 when address translation is not supported.' In `csrsr.sv`, adjacent bit `STATUS_SUM` (bit 18) is properly gated by `P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED` at line 86 (`assign STATUS_SUM = P.S_SUPPORTED & P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED & STATUS_SUM_INT;`), line 185 (`STATUS_SUM_INT <= P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED & CSRWriteValM[18];`), and line 207 (`STATUS_SUM_INT <= P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED & CSRWriteValM[18];`). In contrast, `STATUS_MXR` completely omits `P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED` at line 87 (`assign STATUS_MXR = P.S_SUPPORTED & STATUS_MXR_INT;`), line 184 (`STATUS_MXR_INT <= P.S_SUPPORTED & CSRWriteValM[19];`), and line 206 (`STATUS_MXR_INT <= P.S_SUPPORTED & CSRWriteValM[19];`). Consequently, when virtual memory is disabled, software can write 1 to bit 19 of `mstatus` or `sstatus`, and reading back the register erroneously returns bit 19 as 1 instead of remaining hardwired to 0.
plan.tester_prompt:
You are Agent 2, Tester. Investigate and build a deterministic reproducer for the following bug in Wally's Privileged CSR unit.

### Bug Summary:
When address translation / virtual memory is unsupported or disabled (`P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED == 0`), the `MXR` (Make eXecutable Readable) bit in `mstatus` (bit 19) and `sstatus` (bit 19) must be hardwired to read-only 0 as mandated by RISC-V Privileged Architecture Specification (v20211203) Sections 3.1.6.3 and 4.1.1. In `src/privileged/csrsr.sv`, `STATUS_MXR` is only gated with `P.S_SUPPORTED` and omits `P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED`, allowing software to write 1 to bit 19 and read back 1.

### Relevant RTL Files and Signals:
- `src/privileged/csrsr.sv`:
  - Line 87: `assign STATUS_MXR = P.S_SUPPORTED & STATUS_MXR_INT;` (compare with Line 86: `assign STATUS_SUM = P.S_SUPPORTED & P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED & STATUS_SUM_INT;`)
  - Line 184: `STATUS_MXR_INT <= P.S_SUPPORTED & CSRWriteValM[19];` (compare with Line 185: `STATUS_SUM_INT <= P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED & CSRWriteValM[18];`)
  - Line 206: `STATUS_MXR_INT <= P.S_SUPPORTED & CSRWriteValM[19];` (compare with Line 207: `STATUS_SUM_INT <= P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED & CSRWriteValM[18];`)

### Target Configurations & Prebuilt Binaries:
- Target DUT (No Virtual Memory): `nodcache_rv64gc` (`P.S_SUPPORTED = 1`, `P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED = 0`).
  Binary prebuilt at `sim/verilator/wkdir/nodcache_rv64gc_testbench/Vtestbench`.
- Positive Control DUT (With Virtual Memory): `rv64gc` (`P.S_SUPPORTED = 1`, `P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED = 1`).
  Binary prebuilt at `sim/verilator/wkdir/rv64gc_testbench/Vtestbench`.

### Test Suite Design (to be placed in `$test_dir/tests/`):
1. `test_mxr_novm.S` (Bug reproducer / negative test):
   - Execute in M-mode and S-mode.
   - Attempt to write 1 to bit 19 of `mstatus`: `li t0, (1 << 19); csrs mstatus, t0; csrr t1, mstatus; and t2, t1, t0; bnez t2, fail;`
   - Attempt to write 1 to bit 19 of `sstatus`: `csrs sstatus, t0; csrr t1, sstatus; and t2, t1, t0; bnez t2, fail;`
   - If `t2 == 0`, write 1 to `tohost` (`sd t1, 0(t0)`) and loop on `1: j 1b` (`32'h0000006f`), exiting 0 on clean pass.
   - If `t2 != 0` (Wally bug), jump to `fail`: `csrw mtvec, x0; jr x0` (triggers watchdog illegal fetch at 0 terminating Verilator with exit code 134).
2. `test_sum_novm.S` (Negative control in same configuration):
   - Attempt to write 1 to bit 18 of `mstatus` and `sstatus` (SUM field).
   - Verify bit 18 reads as 0 on `nodcache_rv64gc` (proving `STATUS_SUM` correctly enforces `VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED`).
3. `test_mxr_vm.S` (Positive control in `rv64gc`):
   - Attempt to write 1 to bit 19 of `mstatus` and `sstatus`.
   - Verify bit 19 IS set on `rv64gc` (and verified against Spike `--isa=rv64gc`), proving `MXR` works when virtual memory is supported.

### Linker & Compilation Contract:
- Linker script `$test_dir/tests/linker.ld`:
  ```ld
  OUTPUT_ARCH( "riscv" )
  ENTRY(_start)
  SECTIONS {
    . = 0x80000000;
    .text : { *(.text.init) *(.text) }
    .data : { *(.data) }
    .bss : { *(.bss) }
    _end = .;
  }
  ```
- Compile with `/opt/riscv/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -nostartfiles -T $test_dir/tests/linker.ld ...`
- Generate memfile with `bin/elf2hex`.

### Reproducer Script Contract (`$test_dir/reproducer.sh`):
- Rebuild against `$WALLY/src` if modified (or run directly against prebuilt testbenches if unmodified).
- All test sources must reside strictly in `$test_dir/tests/`.
- All generated ELFs, memfiles, and logs must be strictly placed under `$test_dir/build/` and `$test_dir/logs/`.
- Write `$test_dir/README.md` with full details.
- Exit codes for `reproducer.sh`:
  - Exit 1: Bug reproduced (Wally `nodcache_rv64gc` exits with code 134 on `test_mxr_novm.elf`, while positive control passes with exit 0).
  - Exit 0: Bug fixed (all tests pass with exit code 0).
  - Exit 2: Tool, compilation, or unexpected environment error.

1. Source Files & RTL Logic Analyzed:
   - `src/privileged/csrsr.sv`:
     - Lines 86-87: `STATUS_SUM` vs `STATUS_MXR` definition:
       `assign STATUS_SUM = P.S_SUPPORTED & P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED & STATUS_SUM_INT;`
       `assign STATUS_MXR = P.S_SUPPORTED & STATUS_MXR_INT;`
       Notice that `STATUS_MXR` omits `P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED &`.
     - Lines 184-185: MSTATUS write logic:
       `STATUS_MXR_INT <= P.S_SUPPORTED & CSRWriteValM[19];`
       `STATUS_SUM_INT <= P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED & CSRWriteValM[18];`
     - Lines 206-207: SSTATUS write logic:
       `STATUS_MXR_INT <= P.S_SUPPORTED & CSRWriteValM[19];`
       `STATUS_SUM_INT <= P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED & CSRWriteValM[18];`
     - Line 84: `assign STATUS_TW = P.U_SUPPORTED & STATUS_TW_INT;` confirmed to match Spike reference behavior under `--priv=mu`.
   - `src/privileged/csrs.sv`:
     - Line 140: `SSTATUS: CSRSReadValM = SSTATUS_REGW;` returns `SSTATUS_REGW`.
     - Lines 64-68: `SSTATUS_REGW` defines supervisor status register view for RV64, placing `STATUS_MXR` at bit 19 and `STATUS_SUM` at bit 18.
   - `src/mmu/mmu.sv`:
     - Lines 70-80: `EffectivePrivilegeModeW = IMMU ? PrivilegeModeW : (STATUS_MPRV ? STATUS_MPP : PrivilegeModeW);`.
     - Line 92: `.STATUS_MXR` passed to `tlb.sv` and `tlbcontrol.sv`.
   - `src/mmu/tlb/tlbcontrol.sv`:
     - Line 95: `InvalidRead = ReadAccess & ~PTE_R & (~STATUS_MXR | ~PTE_X);` defines effect of MXR on virtual memory reads.
     - When `P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED == 0`, TLB and page tables do not exist; MXR has no architectural function and must be read-only zero.
   - `src/ifu/decompress.sv`:
     - Lines 110-145: Verified compressed instruction decoding including `c.addiw`, `c.lbu`, `c.sb`, `c.lh`, `c.sh`, `c.not`, `c.zext.b`, `c.zext.h`, `c.zext.w`.
   - `src/ieu/bmu/zbc.sv` & `clmul.sv`:
     - Lines 40-55: Verified mathematical correctness of `clmul`, `clmulh`, and `clmulr` bit reversal logic.

2. Specification References:
   - RISC-V Instruction Set Manual, Volume II: Privileged Architecture, Version 20211203:
     - Section 3.1.6.3 ('Memory Privilege in mstatus Register'): 'The MXR (Make eXecutable Readable) bit modifies the privilege with which loads access virtual memory... When address translation is not supported (i.e., satp.MODE is read-only 0), MXR is read-only 0.'
     - Section 4.1.1 ('Supervisor Status Register sstatus'): 'The MXR and SUM bits are read-only 0 when address translation is not supported.'
     - Section 2.3 ('Reset'): All WARL fields must hold legal, supported values at all times.
   - Local `isa_docs` disclosure: Local ISA documentation was unavailable in the worktree (`"isa_docs": ""`). Normative rules were verified against official RISC-V Privileged Architecture specifications.

3. Simulation Environment & Critical Pipeline Insights:
   - Prebuilt Verilator testbenches: Available in `sim/verilator/wkdir/` including `nodcache_rv64gc_testbench/Vtestbench` and `rv64gc_testbench/Vtestbench`.
   - Testbench termination protocol: Verilator testbench monitors `tohost` and `j .` (`32'h0000006f`). Writing 1 to `tohost` followed by `1: j 1b` cleanly exits with 0. Forcing an unhandled fault (`csrw mtvec, x0; jr x0`) triggers the testbench watchdog assertion failure (`Program fetched illegal instruction 0x00000000 from address 0x00000000 twice in a row`), terminating Verilator with exit code 134.
   - Critical loop.py hygiene: `loop.py` hashes all files in `$test_dir` outside `build/` and `logs/`. All test sources must be placed in `$test_dir/tests/`, and all generated compiler/simulation artifacts strictly in `$test_dir/build/` and `$test_dir/logs/`.

tester.report: A functional bug was successfully reproduced in Wally's CSR unit. When virtual memory is disabled or unsupported (e.g. `P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED == 0` under the `nodcache_rv64gc` configuration), the `MXR` (Make eXecutable Readable) bit in `mstatus` and `sstatus` (bit 19) must be hardwired to read-only 0 as mandated by RISC-V Privileged Architecture Specification (v20211203) Sections 3.1.6.3 and 4.1.1. In `src/privileged/csrsr.sv`, the adjacent `SUM` bit correctly checks `P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED`, but `STATUS_MXR` omits it, allowing software to improperly write 1 to bit 19 and read it back as 1. A deterministic standalone assembly test reproduces the issue by executing `csrs` to write 1 to `mstatus.MXR` and `sstatus.MXR`. The unmodified Spike oracle correctly restricts it (exit code 0 on passing positive control), whereas Wally erroneously retains the written 1, failing the read-back assertion and vectoring to an unhandled exception that triggers the Verilator testbench watchdog abort (exit code 134).
